# TrustyTable

`Data Display` · composition depth: `composite`

Rows and columns as a real HTML table, so a screen reader announces the grid and the headers that name each cell. Columns are declared once and every row supplies its cells by key; a cell is text, text with a quieter second line, or whatever a 'cell-<key>' slot renders. It optionally carries row selection, sortable headers, and a footer housing TrustyPagination and a status line.

The table shows the data it is given and never reorders or slices it — sorting and paging are reported through v-model so the data source can apply them, which is what lets the same component page through 10 rows or 10,000.

**Use it when**
- records share a set of fields and the user compares them across rows.

**Don't use it for**
- laying a page out in rows and columns: that is CSS grid's job, not a table's
- hierarchical or nested records: use TrustyTree
- a list of one field per record: use TrustyTree, or plain markup
- picking one value from many: use TrustySelect

```ts
import { TrustyTable } from '@louislp/trusty-ui'
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `columns` | `TrustyTableColumn[]` | *required* | The columns, left to right. |
| `rows` | `TrustyTableRow[]` | *required* | The rows of the page currently on screen. |
| `label` | `string` | — | Names the table for screen readers, as a visually hidden `<caption>`. Optional, but worth setting when the surrounding page doesn't already say what the rows are. |
| `selectable` | `boolean` | `false` | Adds the leading checkbox column and the select-all box in the header. |
| `emptyLabel` | `string` | `"No items yet"` | Shown in place of the body when there are no rows. |
| `total` | `number` | — | Rows in the whole collection, across every page. Setting it renders the footer — the status line, plus pagination once there is a second page. |
| `itemsPerPage` | `number` | `10` | Rows on one page. Drives both the pagination and the status line. |
| `selected` | `(string \| number)[]` | `[]` |  |
| `sort` | `TrustyTableSort` | `undefined` |  |
| `page` | `number` | `1` |  |

## Events

- `update:page` — `[value: number]`
- `update:selected` — `[value: (string \| number)[]]`
- `update:sort` — `[value: TrustyTableSort \| undefined]`

## Examples in Storybook

- Default — Columns, rows, and one slot-filled Actions column. No footer without a `total`.
- Paginated — `total` brings the footer: the status line, and pagination past page one. Live — the page drives which slice of the collection is handed to `rows`, exactly as a consuming app would.
- Selectable — Checkbox column plus select-all. Disabled rows sit it out, and the status line switches to the selection count. Live — tick the boxes.
- Sorted — Sortable headers report the column and direction through `v-model:sort`; the table reorders nothing itself. Live — this story sorts its own rows off that model, which is the job a consuming app (or its backend) picks up.
- Empty — No rows: the headers stay so the shape of the data is still legible, and the checkbox column drops out.
- PlainText — Text-only cells — every column plain, no descriptions and no slots.
